correctness.rationale: The gradient intertwining identity is exact, and the oriented cycle differences are precisely all zero-sum edge vectors. The nonnegative dipole transport identity preserves weighted ell-one cost. Each dipole right derivative F_ij is computed exactly at zero and at the two supports; a sufficiently small Euler step preserves their signs and yields exact norm change h F_ij. Contractive dipoles therefore imply contraction for every vector by triangle inequality and for every time by Euler products. Distance-three and -four pair inequalities have zero aggregate slack, yielding constant pair sums and n>=7 weight rigidity. For n=6 the distance-two inequalities imply all adjacent inequalities; n<=5 follows by explicit pair types. An exact-arithmetic checker and independent full matrix exponentials corroborated the boundary and witness statements.

value.rationale: This theorem completely describes which independent anisotropic variation weights are compatible with universally variation-diminishing heat diffusion on finite cycles. The exceptional six-cycle cone and immediate all-positive-weight rigidity at seven edges supply a sharp nontrivial transition; the effective exact finite-dimensional test and explicit instability dipoles can guide stable graph-filter design. It is not a restatement of uniform Markov contractivity or a routine parameter substitution.
